Cyberattacks are going parabolic, per Bridgewater.

Estimated total cyber incidents have more than doubled since late summer, from about 4,000 a year to nearly 10,000 on a 60-day annualized basis. Over most of the past decade they rose slowly, from about 1,500 in 2017 to roughly 4,000 by mid-2026.

The surge began around the release of the open weights for GLM-5.3, a Chinese AI model from Zhipu AI. Anthropic’s red team had found it could build working cyber exploits. Verified AI-driven cyber incidents have jumped from near zero to more than 200 a year in the same period, including campaigns in which AI agents stole Korean bank and card data.

The San Diego City Council voted unanimously to end the city’s license plate reader program, turning off about 500 Flock cameras.

The vote makes San Diego the largest US city to shut down its Flock network. Police say the cameras will go dark and their data will be deleted within 24 hours. In a separate 5-2 vote, the council also suspended the city’s “Smart Streetlights,” which record video used by police.

The program lost support after reports that a San Diego police officer may have used the cameras to track a domestic violence victim he allegedly had an inappropriate relationship with. A misidentification also left an innocent man jailed for a month. Three council members who backed the technology last year switched sides.

San Diego just voted to shut down its Flock license plate camera program and turn off about 500 cameras.

Nvidia $NVDA is moving up pay raises and stock grants to hold on to employees after Jensen Huang’s exit, per WIRED.

At her first all-hands meeting as interim CEO on Wednesday, Colette Kress told staff they’ll get raises and additional equity in December, months earlier than planned. Nvidia wants to “take care of each and every single employee that is here,” she said.

Pay was the top issue among about 700 questions employees submitted before the meeting. The next most common request was more transparency from the board, which the announcement didn’t address. Thousands of employees have reportedly lobbied for Huang’s return, but board chair Harvey Jones said Huang won’t be invited back.

Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians as the world’s largest religious group by 2035, according to new Pew Research Center projections.

In 2020 there were about 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims. By 2035, Pew projects about 2.57 billion Muslims and 2.52 billion Christians, and by 2070 more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under 3 billion Christians.

The main driver is birth rates, not conversion. Muslim women averaged 3.1 children in 2020–2025, compared with 2.5 for Christian women. “It’s the babies,” said Pew demographer Conrad Hackett.

The market doesn’t owe you a trade every day.

That’s one of the biggest lessons I see traders who started after 2020 struggling with right now.

Meme stocks, crypto, and the parabolic moves in 2021 and 2025 spoiled a lot of people. They got used to trading every day and growing their accounts FAST.

Now this 2026 market is punishing those same habits.

I’ve traded for 16 years. The people who survive these markets are willing to sit in cash for days or weeks if there’s nothing worth risking money on.

Cash is king. You don’t have to make back your losses this week. You don’t have to catch the exact bottom.

You just need enough capital left to take advantage when the market turns.

The moment you truly accept that any trade can go against you, things change. You quit sizing too big and you quit breaking your rules every session. That’s when discipline starts, and that’s when you start to last.

Now the opposite. You enter a trade and assume the market owes you the move. Confidence turns into overconfidence, and you take on more risk than you planned. You skip the question that matters: “What if I’m wrong, and what does that cost me?” It can always happen, and when it does, it can hurt.

Hold too much size through that and the account takes a hard hit. Your focus flips from growing the account to repairing it. You drop your plan and start chasing the loss back.

So keep your size in check. Don’t walk into any trade sure it will work, because nothing in this market is guaranteed.

Accept that and you’ll see your results get better.
